Zero-shot learning vision-language models have gained significant attention in recent years due to their ability to perform well on unseen tasks without explicit training data (Peng Gao et al., 2023). However, the performance of these models can be limited by the quality of the pre-training data and the fine-tuning process (Laith Alzubaidi et al., 2021). One approach to improving the performance of zero-shot learning vision-language models is to use feature adapters, which can adapt the pre-trained model to the specific task at hand (Peng Gao et al., 2023). This approach has been shown to be effective in improving the performance of vision-language models on various tasks, including image classification and object detection (Peng Gao et al., 2023). Another approach is to use prompting methods, which can provide the model with task-specific information and improve its performance (Pengfei Liu et al., 2022). Despite the progress made in zero-shot learning vision-language models, there are still several challenges and limitations associated with these models. One of the main challenges is the lack of data, which can limit the performance of the model (Laith Alzubaidi et al., 2023). Another challenge is the need for large amounts of computational resources, which can make it difficult to train and fine-tune these models (Wijegunarathna et al., 2023). In terms of applications, zero-shot learning vision-language models have been used in various fields, including medical imaging (Jun Ma et al., 2024) and natural language processing (Pengfei Liu et al., 2022). These models have been shown to be effective in improving the performance of various tasks, including image classification, object detection, and text classification (Peng Gao et al., 2023). In conclusion, zero-shot learning vision-language models have made significant progress in recent years, but there are still several challenges and limitations associated with these models.
